chapter: Leaving Duke and the Hollywood years
title: Why he left Ellington in 1942
summary: Wartime train travel meant sitting in the aisle, he met the woman who became his wife in Los Angeles and stayed, having lost admiration for Duke after the incident about his father; they remained friendly.

story.theme_name: Meeting, marrying and raising a family
story.community_name: Meeting, courting and marrying: musicians' love lives

blocks.x: Well, the war -- you know, we used to have, like I told you, the Pullman and all that and they couldn't get that anymore and the last job we had to get a seat anywhere we could on a train, since I was sitting in the
aisle, and then Miss Scrabble Lou --
I called her Miss Scrabble Lou. (That's when you met your wife, you (unintelligible)?)
You met her in Los Angeles?

Yeah. So I said, 'Why go through all that trouble? Come back here and stay.' So that's the way it was. So I said, 'Well, now, I've had it.' And then, because I had lost all the admiration I had for Duke since he acted like that about my father, you know. So I didn't care. He didn't talk to me, I didn't talk to him. I didn't even tell him goodbye. But that was it.
But we were friends, you know. There was never no hard feelings or anything, or we brought up old past things -- nothing like that. We just -- we talked every time we saw each other.
